Closed length-n walks in the 16^4-state overlap graph bijectively encode labelled configurations fixed by M² for n≥5; the 4^4 fixed graph similarly encodes Fix(M). Rebuilding the full directed graphs from the displayed local truth constraints gives exactly 65,536 states/102,400 edges and 256 states/320 edges. Independent iterative SCC decomposition gives recurrent cyclic components of sizes 1,1,778 (2202 internal edges) and 1,1,24 (36 edges), so the trace identities for all n≥5 follow, not merely for sampled circumferences. The 778- and 24-state blocks are strongly connected with loops, thus primitive. Independent arbitrary-integer calculations on v=R^80 1 verify 264157 v_i<100000(Rv)_i<264158 v_i and 156485 v_i<100000(Rv)_i<156486 v_i coordinatewise, giving exact Perron intervals. The published and independently reconstructed prism Lucas/period-two formulas have growth φ and φ². As α<φ<φ²<β, the opposite fixed- and primitive-two-cycle exponential comparisons follow. All counts concern immediate periodic labelled states, not attraction basins; short n checks do not substitute for the transfer proof.

value.rationale: A sharp all-circumference two-cycle transfer and rigorous 778-state Perron enclosure expose an unexpected same-degree, same-size change of dynamical populations: GP(n,2) has exponentially fewer equilibria but more primitive oscillations than the prism GP(n,1). The exact growth rate β is a natural dynamical invariant not determined by earlier fixed-state tables or a ten-vertex census. The contrast is a mathematically motivated complete-family phenomenon, not an arbitrary small graph count.

limitations: No claim about basins or transients, n<5 excluded because graph neighbor degeneracy.
Spectral enclosure is finite exact arithmetic tied to fully specified graph, not a mere decimal eigenvalue estimate.
